detail.longDescription: I have cloned a Git repository partially using: git clone --filter=blob:none URL The .git directory is small and everything is fine. However, when I go back in history, old file versions are downloaded and added to .git . How can I get rid of them, again? Another scenario: I have cloned a Git repository, the .git is huge (> 1 GB), but the source tree is small (around 10 MB). Can I get rid of old blobs from upstream? However, I already added private branches and want to maintain their contents. The solutions I found remove large files from commits and thus alter the history or suggest a fresh clone. All suggestions with gc and prune won't help, since those old blobs are referenced by the history and thus gc won't remove them.
